# BaZi vs MBTI and Modern Personality Tests: What Each Can and Cannot Tell You

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/bazi-vs-personality-tests
Updated: 2026-09-16

BaZi Basics

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-09-16
Sooner or later everyone curious about BaZi asks the modern question: how does it compare to MBTI, Big Five, DISC, or whatever assessment their workplace administered last year? The comparison is genuinely interesting — not because one "wins," but because the two families answer different questions with different failure modes.

## The method difference is the whole story

A personality questionnaire measures how you describe yourself today. Its input is self-report, which brings the known weaknesses: mood effects, social desirability, the fact that your answers change as your self-image does. Test-retest studies of type-based instruments famously show many people landing in a different box months later.

BaZi's input is your birth data — fixed, objective, and impossible to game. Its computation is perfectly repeatable: the same birth moment yields the same chart forever. The controversial step is different: whether the mapping from chart to character is valid is exactly the claim modern psychometrics would demand evidence for, and classical literature answers with a millennium of accumulated case reasoning rather than controlled trials. An honest practitioner says so.

## What each does well

- Questionnaires excel at snapshotting your current self-concept in a shared vocabulary — useful for team conversations and self-reflection right now.

- BaZi excels at what self-report cannot do at all: it is stable (a lifelong reference, not a mood-dependent snapshot), it is structural (strengths and needs expressed as element balances with prescribed compensations — colours, directions, timing), and it has a time axis. No personality test has an opinion about when: BaZi's luck cycles (大运) and annual years (流年) are half the system.

BaZi also scales to relationships and environment: the same chart drives compatibility patterns, room allocation, and date selection — one framework from personality to floor plan.

## What neither should claim

A four-letter type does not predict job performance well, and a BaZi chart does not condemn or guarantee anyone. Both are lenses. The classical tradition is explicit that the chart is one factor among several (一命二运三风水…); good modern practice holds personality tests to the same modesty.

## Using them together

The practical move is not either/or. Take the questionnaire's snapshot of how you currently operate; take BaZi's structural map of what feeds and drains you and when the terrain shifts. Where they agree, you have convergence from two independent methods — worth acting on. Where they disagree, you have the most interesting question of all: is the difference your circumstances masking your structure, or the structure claim failing for you? Either answer teaches something a single instrument could not.

Your chart — Day Master, strength, favourable elements, and the ten-year cycle you are in now — computes in under a minute below, every line citing the classical rule behind it. Bring your MBTI letters and compare for yourself.

# Bed Direction in Feng Shui: Eight House Rules for HDB and Condo Beds

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/bed-direction-guide
Updated: 2026-10-08

Feng Shui Basics

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-10-08
Bed direction in feng shui is the compass direction your head points to when you lie on the bed. It is chosen from the auspicious directions of your Eight House (八宅) kua, after the form rules about the wall, the door and the window have been satisfied. Form decides which walls are allowed; the compass ranks the survivors.

## How do I find which direction is best for my head?

Two sets of rules sit side by side, and they are easy to confuse: compass rules (which of the eight directions suits you, from your kua) and form rules (what the door, windows and walls physically do to the bed). Classical doctrine puts form first, so a perfect compass direction does not redeem a bed that the door slams into.

The compass part is mechanical. Your birth year and sex give a kua (命卦), one of eight trigrams, and the kua puts you in one of two groups. The 八宅大遊年 line transformation (the 八宅明鏡 tradition) then labels every direction with one of eight stars. The engine scores them as follows.

Star | Meaning in the engine | Score | 

生氣 | vitality | +3.0 | 

天醫 | health | +2.5 | 

延年 | relationships and longevity | +2.0 | 

伏位 | stable seat | +1.0 | 

禍害 | mishaps | -1.0 | 

六煞 | six killings | -1.5 | 

五鬼 | five ghosts | -2.0 | 

絕命 | life-severing | -3.0 | 

The four positive stars are the "auspicious" directions and the four negative ones are the ones to keep your head away from.

Key facts

- The 八宅 system has 8 directions, each labelled with 1 of 8 stars scored from +3.0 (生氣) to -3.0 (絕命).
- There are 2 kua groups: 東四命 (坎 離 震 巽) and 西四命 (乾 坤 艮 兌).
- A man born in 1988 and a woman born in 1988 both have kua 震; a man born in 1990 has kua 坎 and a woman born in 1990 has kua 艮.
- The headboard direction is where the top of the head points while lying down, not where the feet point.
- A kua 坎 person's best head direction is southeast (巽, 生氣, +3.0), followed by east (震, 天醫, +2.5).
- The engine cites the rule behind each score, for example "命卦 坎 → 離宮 (S) is 延年", from 八宅大遊年.

The eight positions for kua 坎: southeast 生氣, east 天醫, south 延年, north 伏位, west 禍害, northwest 六煞, northeast 五鬼, southwest 絕命

## Which directions suit kua 坎?

The figure above and the table below show the eight positions for kua 坎. Here the 巽 (southeast) wall is the best head position, then 震 (east), 離 (south) and 坎 (north). The remaining four walls are the ones to avoid for the head.

Direction | Trigram | Star | Score | 

SE | 巽 | 生氣 | +3.0 | 

E | 震 | 天醫 | +2.5 | 

S | 離 | 延年 | +2.0 | 

N | 坎 | 伏位 | +1.0 | 

W | 兌 | 禍害 | -1.0 | 

NW | 乾 | 六煞 | -1.5 | 

NE | 艮 | 五鬼 | -2.0 | 

SW | 坤 | 絕命 | -3.0 | 

Each kua gets its own table, which is why a copy-and-paste "best direction" list from the internet is wrong for most readers. The same wall that is 生氣 for kua 坎 is 禍害 for kua 乾.

## What are the form rules for a bed, in order of severity?

These are conventions of the classical form school, applied as penalties by the engine (method note: the penalty sizes are the engine's, the rules are traditional).

- Solid wall behind the headboard. The head needs backing (靠). A headboard against glass, including a bay window, fails this rule. If a window wall is unavoidable, use a tall solid headboard and heavy curtains, or keep the pillow on a solid wall with the glass on the bed's flank.

- Stay out of the door's entry line (門沖床). The strip of space the doorway projects into the room should not run onto the bed, least of all onto the pillow. A wardrobe, tall shelf or desk placed between door and bed intercepts the line.

- Feet not pointing squarely at the door. A foot bench or low cabinet settles mild cases.

- Commanding position. From the pillow you should see the door, ideally diagonally. A door hidden behind your head is the pattern to avoid.

- Bed crowded behind the door leaf. When the opened door stands beside the pillow, add a doorstop and a bedside table as buffer.

- No mirror facing the bed, nothing heavy overhead, such as a beam or shelf over the pillow, and no toilet on the headboard wall.

## How does this work in an HDB flat or condo?

The room you are in decides what is possible, so measure it before you decide anything.

- Facing and compass. Stand inside the unit at the main door and look out; that is the unit's facing. For the bed, what matters is the compass direction of the headboard wall, which you read with a phone compass held flat in the room. Read the plan of your unit, not the block, because a flat's bedrooms point in different directions.

- Which walls are candidates. List the walls that can take a bed head, strike out the ones that fail the form rules, then rank what remains by score. A wall shared with a toilet fails rule 6; if it is the only solid wall, the tool flags the defect and gives its remedy instead of hiding it.

- Condo glass. Floor-to-ceiling glazing on a bedroom wall fails rule 1 for that wall, however good its direction scores.

Two partners often belong to opposite groups. A man born in 1990 has kua 坎 (East group) and a woman born in 1990 has kua 艮 (West group). Their good directions do not overlap, so the couple picks the wall that serves the partner under more strain and compensates the other with their side of the bed.

## What does a worked example look like?

Take the fictional 王大明, born 1988-03-15, whose kua is 震 (東四命). His eight directions from 八宅大遊年 are:

- South (離) is 生氣, +3.0.

- North (坎) is 天醫, +2.5.

- Southeast (巽) is 延年, +2.0.

- East (震) is 伏位, +1.0.

- Southwest (坤) is 禍害, -1.0.

- Northeast (艮) is 六煞, -1.5.

- Northwest (乾) is 五鬼, -2.0.

- West (兌) is 絕命, -3.0.

Suppose his bedroom has three possible headboard walls: south (solid), west (a window wall) and north (door on the same side). He strikes out the west wall twice: it is the 絕命 direction and it is glass. The north wall has the second-best score but runs into the door's entry line, so it needs a wardrobe screen. The south wall scores +3.0 and has solid backing, so the pillow goes south, and the commanding-position check decides which end of the wall the bed sits at.

If he preferred north, the annual layer also matters: in 2027 the 五黃 star sits in the north palace, and the flying stars guide explains how to weigh that overlay.

## Sources and method

- Kua and eight-star labelling: 八宅大遊年 (trigram line transformation), in the 八宅明鏡 tradition.

- Star scores (+3.0 to -3.0): the engine's weights for the eight stars (method note).

- Form rules (solid backing, 門沖床, commanding position): classical form-school conventions, applied by the engine as penalties (method note).

- Annual overlay: the 五黃 and the 太歲 and 歲破 positions follow 協紀辨方書 and the annual flying-star order.

- Year boundary for charts: the 立春 convention of the 子平 calendar.

Find your own kua and directions with the free reading at /start, or trace your bedroom, mark the door and windows, and see all four walls scored in the home tool at /fengshui.

# The Ten Day Masters (日主): Which One Are You?

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/day-masters-explained
Updated: 2026-09-16

BaZi Basics

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-09-16
In a BaZi chart, one character stands for you: the Heavenly Stem of your day pillar, called the Day Master (日主 or 日元). Everything else in the chart — the other seven characters, the luck cycles, the annual years — is read in relation to it. There are exactly ten possibilities, one for each stem, and each is one of the Five Elements in either yang (阳) or yin (阴) polarity.

## The ten, in one pass

- 甲 (jiǎ) — yang wood. The tall tree: upright, principled, slow to bend, grows in one direction. Thrives with room to grow; struggles when boxed in.

- 乙 (yǐ) — yin wood. The vine or flowering grass: flexible, adaptive, finds a way around obstacles rather than through them.

- 丙 (bǐng) — yang fire. The sun: warm, visible, generous with energy, at its best in the open. Dislikes being ignored more than being opposed.

- 丁 (dīng) — yin fire. The lamp flame: focused, penetrating, quietly persistent. Reads people well; burns steadily rather than brightly.

- 戊 (wù) — yang earth. The mountain: stable, protective, hard to move — a reliability that can shade into stubbornness.

- 己 (jǐ) — yin earth. The field soil: nurturing, absorbent, cultivating. Works on people and projects patiently, from below.

- 庚 (gēng) — yang metal. The axe or raw ore: decisive, dutiful, cuts through. Justice-minded; blunt when unpolished.

- 辛 (xīn) — yin metal. The jewel: refined, precise, image-aware. Small, hard, and sharper than it looks.

- 壬 (rén) — yang water. The river or sea: expansive, resourceful, always moving, hard to contain.

- 癸 (guǐ) — yin water. The rain or dew: subtle, perceptive, seeps in everywhere; the quiet strategist of the ten.

These portraits are a doorway, not a verdict. Two 丙 fire people can live very different lives, because the Day Master is only the subject of the sentence — the rest of the chart supplies the verbs.

## Strength changes everything

Classical technique first asks whether your Day Master is strong (身强) or weak (身弱): does the season of your birth month feed it, and do the other characters support or drain it? The answer flips the whole reading. A strong Day Master welcomes challenge and output (the elements that drain it become productive); a weak one needs support first (the elements that feed it become the medicine). This strength assessment is a rule-based computation — month-season weighting plus rooted support — not an intuition, and it is the foundation the next article builds on: your favourable elements, or 用神.

## Find yours precisely

Because the day pillar runs on an unbroken 60-day cycle, you cannot guess your Day Master from your birthday — it has to be computed, with the day boundary handled correctly (the traditional day starts at 子时, 11 pm). The free reading below computes it exactly and tells you not just which Day Master you are, but whether it is strong or weak and what follows from that.

---

# Eight House (八宅) Basics: Your Four Good and Four Bad Directions

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/eight-house-directions
Updated: 2026-09-16

Fengshui

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-09-16
Of all the classical fengshui schools, Eight House (八宅) is the most personal: it starts not from the building but from you. From your birth year and sex it derives a life gua (命卦) — one of eight trigrams — and from that, every compass direction becomes one of eight qualities, four auspicious and four inauspicious. It is the system behind "sleep with your head pointing this way" and "face this direction at your desk."

## Your life gua and your group

The 命卦 is computed from the birth year (with the 立春 boundary, as always) by a digital-root method, with separate formulas for men and women. The eight guas split into two families:

- East group (东四命): 坎 (water), 离 (fire), 震 (wood), 巽 (wood)

- West group (西四命): 乾 (metal), 坤 (earth), 艮 (earth), 兑 (metal)

East-group people share the same four good directions (N, S, E, SE); West-group people share the other four (W, NW, SW, NE). Which of the four is which quality differs by gua — that mapping is the 大游年 table, and it is pure lookup, no judgment involved.

## The eight qualities

The four auspicious:

- 生气 (Sheng Qi) — vitality; the strongest. Best for the headboard, the desk facing, the front door.

- 天医 (Tian Yi) — the heavenly doctor; health and recovery.

- 延年 (Yan Nian) — longevity and relationships; steady support.

- 伏位 (Fu Wei) — the home position; calm and stability.

The four inauspicious, in worsening order: 祸害 (mishaps) → 六煞 (six killings) → 五鬼 (five ghosts) → 绝命 (severed fate). The practical rule is not fear but allocation: put activity in your good directions (sleeping, studying, facing) and storage or utility in the bad ones.

## Using it in a real home

- Headboard direction first. Sleeping is a third of your life; pointing the head toward 生气, 天医 or 延年 is the highest-leverage move the school offers.

- Desk facing second. You face a direction for hours; make it an auspicious one.

- Couples with opposite groups are normal. One east, one west is common — the classical resolution is to favour the person carrying the heavier load in that room, and to compensate the other elsewhere (their side of the bed, their study corner).

- The house has a gua too. A dwelling's sitting direction makes it an east or west house; matching person to house is a bonus, not a requirement — room allocation does the real work.

## Where 八宅 sits among the schools

Eight House answers "which directions suit this person"; Flying Stars (玄空飞星) answers "what energy occupies this sector of this building in this period"; form-school doctrine answers "what does the physical layout do" (doors, beds, sightlines). Serious practice layers all three, with form first (形势为先) when they conflict. A reading that shows you the layer and the rule behind each recommendation lets you check the work — which is exactly how the engine behind this site is built. The free reading computes your 命卦, your full eight-direction map, and the bed and desk directions that follow.

# The Five Elements in a BaZi Chart: Balance, the 生克 Cycles, and What Excess Means

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/five-elements-cycles
Updated: 2026-09-19

BaZi treats a chart as a five-element ecosystem: 木 wood, 火 fire, 土 earth, 金 metal, 水
water. Every stem and branch — including the hidden stems — carries an element, and a weighted
count of all of them gives the chart's element balance. The single most important habit
when reading the bar chart: balance beats abundance. The tallest bar is the heaviest
influence, not the best one; the shortest bar is where the ecosystem is thin.

## The two cycles

The elements interact along two fixed cycles. The feeding cycle 相生 runs wood→fire→
earth→metal→water→wood: each element generates the next. The controlling cycle 相克 runs
wood→earth→water→fire→metal→wood: each element checks another, the way a dam checks a river. Both
cycles are neutral machinery — control is not bad, it is structure. Trouble appears when weights
are lopsided: a very heavy element crushes the one it controls (a friction), and a very weak
element cannot feed the one downstream of it (a gap).

## The five roles around your Day Master

Relative to YOUR Day Master's element, the other four take fixed roles: the element that
feeds you is your resource (印); the one you produce is your output (食傷); the one
you control is your wealth (財); the one that controls you is your authority /
pressure (官殺); your own element is your peers (比劫). These five roles are exactly
what the ten gods refine one level further — the element wheel
and the ten-god chart are the same picture at two zoom levels.

## What the frictions mean in life

A reading names each live friction in one sentence — "growth overruns stability: plans trample
routines" for heavy wood against earth, or "stability dams flow: communication gets blocked" for
heavy earth against water. These are recurring THEMES, not events: once named, each is manageable —
usually by strengthening the buffer element that drains the aggressor and feeds the victim.

## Health correspondences and daily levers

Traditional five-element medicine maps each element to organ systems — wood to liver and eyes,
fire to heart, earth to digestion, metal to lungs and skin, water to kidneys and bones. A very
weak or very excessive element marks the systems worth caring for; it is a reference layer, never
medical advice. The practical levers are gentler: your
favourable elements (用神) translate into colours to wear,
sectors of the home to use, and industries where effort converts efficiently — the everyday
interface to a chart's element balance.

---

# Flying Stars 2027 (丁未年): Annual Chart, 太歲 and 五黃 for SG and MY Homes

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/flying-stars-2027
Updated: 2026-10-08

Flying Stars

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-10-08
Flying stars (玄空飛星) are a feng shui method that places nine numbered stars across the centre and eight compass sectors of a building, and re-deals the annual stars every year at 立春. In 2027, a 丁未 year, star 9 enters the centre and the 五黃 star 5 sits in the north.

## What does the 2027 annual chart look like?

The annual chart is the same for every building on earth: it depends only on the year, not on your address. What differs is which of your rooms falls in which sector. The engine that powers our home readings gives this distribution for 2027.

The 2027 annual flying-star grid: 9 in the centre, 1 northwest, 2 west, 3 northeast, 4 south, 5 north, 6 southwest, 7 east, 8 southeast
Palace | Direction | Star | Element | Quality in the engine (period 9) | 

中 | centre | 9 | 火 | 當運旺星, score +2.0 | 

乾 | NW | 1 | 水 | 生氣星 (next period), +1.5 | 

兌 | W | 2 | 土 | 二黑 病符, illness star, -1.5 | 

艮 | NE | 3 | 木 | 三碧 是非, conflict star, -1.0 | 

離 | S | 4 | 木 | 平星, 0.0 | 

坎 | N | 5 | 土 | 五黃 廉貞, most afflictive, -2.0 | 

坤 | SW | 6 | 金 | 吉白星, +0.5 | 

震 | E | 7 | 金 | 平星, 0.0 | 

巽 | SE | 8 | 土 | 退氣星, -0.5 | 

Key facts

- The 2027 annual chart starts at 立春 on 2027-02-04 and runs to 立春 on 2028-02-04.
- Star 9 is in the centre and star 5 (五黃) is in the north palace 坎.
- The 太歲 sits at 未, southwest, in the 202.5° to 217.5° arc.
- The 歲破 sits at 丑, northeast, in the 22.5° to 37.5° arc.
- The 三煞 occupy the west frame 申酉戌, the arc from 232.5° to 307.5°.
- The 五黃 scores -2.0 in the engine, the lowest of the nine stars.

## When does the flying-star year change?

At 立春, 2027-02-04, not on 1 January and not at Chinese New Year. A condo owner who finishes a renovation on 2 February 2027 is still working in the 丙午 year, with a different chart. The year pillar shows the switch: a date of 2027-01-20 carries 丙午, and 2027-02-10 carries 丁未.

The centre star moves one step each year. In 2026 the centre star is 1, in 2027 it is 9 and in 2028 it is 8. The 五黃 therefore travels: south (離) in 2026, north (坎) in 2027 and southwest (坤) in 2028. Anything you plan across the 4 February boundary should be checked against both charts.

## Which annual afflictions apply in 2027?

Three year-spirits (年神) rotate with the year branch, and they are separate from the numbered stars. These positions are derived from the 年神 rules in 協紀辨方書 (method note: the engine's public output is the star chart, and these three are derived from the rules for the 丁未 year).

- 太歲 (Grand Duke) sits on the year branch. For 未 that is southwest, the arc SW1.

- 歲破 (Year Breaker) sits on the branch opposite the year branch. Opposite 未 is 丑, northeast, the arc NE1.

- 三煞 (Three Killings) for a 亥卯未 year sit on the opposite frame: the west, 申酉戌. That is SW3, W2 and NW1 in the 24-mountain ring.

Together with the north 五黃, the sectors to treat carefully in 2027 are southwest, northeast, the western arc and north. For the 五黃 sector itself the engine's remedy table gives the traditional answer: place metal there (brass, a six-coin string or a metal pendulum clock) to drain the earth star, and keep it quiet (method note: engine remedy table). The practical rule is the traditional one: avoid structural work that breaks the ground or the wall (動土) in those sectors during the year. Assembling flat-pack furniture is not 動土; hacking tiles, hacking walls and drilling for new points is.

## How do I read the chart for an HDB flat or condo?

Use the unit plan, not the block. Stand inside the unit at the main door looking out; that direction is the facing. Then overlay the nine-palace grid on the floor plan of your own unit, with north at the real compass north, and see which rooms fall in which palace. Neighbouring units in the same block face the same way but have different room layouts, so their palace map differs.

Two Singapore and Malaysia points matter in practice. First, a single flat can put its rooms in three or four different palaces, so the annual chart is read room by room and not for the flat as a whole. Second, a condo unit with a glass balcony wall has a clear facing but a looser boundary, so the room outline you trace in the tool decides which palace the balcony belongs to.

## What does a worked example show?

Take the fictional 王大明, born 1988-03-15, kua 震, East group. His Eight House map says his 生氣 direction is south (離), his 天醫 is north (坎), his 延年 is southeast (巽), and east (震) is 伏位, the stable seat.

Now overlay 2027:

- South, his best direction, carries the annual 4, a neutral 平星 at 0.0. The sector stays usable and loses nothing; it just gains no annual boost.

- North, his 天醫 direction, carries 五黃 at -2.0. A study or bed that relies on that wall is working against the annual star for this year. The natal and personal layers still count, but the year layer is the heaviest single annual penalty.

- East, his 伏位 seat, carries the neutral 7.

- Southwest holds both the 太歲 and the annual 6, a favourable 吉白星 at +0.5. The 太歲 is the more specific warning for ground-breaking, so the rule is to keep it free of structural work even though the star is kind.

The conclusion is not "move out" or "avoid north". It is the overlay: in 2027, keep construction away from north, northeast, southwest and the west frame, and check the sleeping direction against the form rules in the bed direction guide.

## Why are annual stars a layer and not the whole story?

The annual chart sits on top of the building's natal chart, which comes from its facing and construction period under 沈氏玄空學, including the 替卦 replacement stars used for 兼向 facings. It also sits above your personal Eight House directions from 八宅. A sector can be natal-strong and annually afflicted, or the reverse. The reading that matters is the overlay of all three, and each layer should show the rule that produced it.

The home tool computes all three layers for a plan you trace and produces a renovation-timing table with each rule cited. Use it to see which of your rooms fall in the 2027 afflicted sectors.

## Sources and method

- Annual star chart: the nine-star flying order with the centre star set at each 立春; the engine's output, listed in the table above.

- Star qualities in period 9: the engine's own scoring of each star (method note), not a classical table.

- 太歲, 歲破 and 三煞 positions: the 年神 position rules of 協紀辨方書, applied to the 丁未 year branch.

- Natal chart and 替卦: 沈氏玄空學, on the 兼向 replacement stars.

- Personal directions in the worked example: 八宅大遊年, the 八宅明鏡 tradition.

- Year boundary: 立春 as the solar term that opens the year in the 子平 calendar.

Trace your own floor plan in the home tool at /fengshui, or begin with the free personal reading at /start.

# How to Read a Four Pillars Chart: Stems, Branches, Hidden Stems and the Four Palaces

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/four-pillars-explained
Updated: 2026-09-19

A BaZi chart is eight characters arranged in four columns — the four pillars (四柱) of
the year, month, day and hour of birth. Each pillar is written as two characters: a heavenly
stem (天干) on top and an earthly branch (地支) below. The stem is the visible, declared
energy of that pillar; the branch is its foundation, and the year branch carries the zodiac animal
most people know their birth year by.

## The Day Master — the character that is you

The stem of the day pillar is the 日主 Day Master: the character the whole chart is read
against. Every other character is classified by its relationship to it — those relationships are
the ten gods. The day pillar is usually drawn outlined in a
chart for this reason: its stem is you, and its branch is the spouse palace (配偶宮), the
seat of marriage and domestic life.

## Hidden stems — the ingredients inside each branch

Every branch stores one to three hidden stems (藏干): extra elements sealed inside the
pillar like ingredients in a pantry. 亥 hides 壬 water and 甲 wood; 辰 hides 戊 earth, 乙 wood and
癸 water. A chart that looks light in some element on the surface may carry it hidden in the
branches — which is why serious element counts always weigh hidden stems, and why a Day Master
with no visible support can still be "rooted" (通根) if its element hides in a branch below.

## The four pillars are also the four palaces

Classical doctrine reads the same four columns a second way, as the 宮位 four palaces —
a timeline and a map of relationships at once:

- Year pillar 年柱 — ages 0–15 · ancestry, childhood environment, first impressions.

- Month pillar 月柱 — ages 16–32 · parents, early adulthood, and the career
headquarters: the month is the strongest single influence on the chart's climate.

- Day pillar 日柱 — ages 33–48 · the self (stem) and the spouse (branch).

- Hour pillar 時柱 — ages 49+ · children, students, works, late-life luck.

So the ten gods say WHAT an energy is; the palace it sits in says WHEN it peaks and WHERE it
plays out. A wealth god in the month palace colours the career; the same god in the hour palace
colours the later years and the children. Whenever a luck decade or a passing year clashes or
combines with a pillar, it is that palace's life-area that feels it.

## What else a pillar carries

Each pillar also has a 納音 melodic element — the poetic sixty-cycle name like 屋上土
"earth on the roof" — and a 長生 life-stage, the Day Master's phase in that pillar
(birth → peak → decline). These are flavour and vitality readings layered over the structure, not
verdicts. Symbolic stars (神煞) such as 天乙貴人 the
Nobleman or 文昌 the scholar star also attach to specific pillars, and are read in the palace they
land in: a Nobleman in the year palace means helpful elders early in life.

Read in this order — Day Master first, then the month for climate, then each palace — a four
pillars chart stops being eight mysterious characters and becomes a structured record: who, in
what season, supported or drained by what, and when each theme takes the stage.

---

# How Chinese Baby Names Are Scored: 用神, 五格, 三才, Meaning, Sound and Gender

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/how-chinese-baby-names-are-scored
Updated: 2026-10-08

Naming

By BaziMaster 2026-10-08 Updated 2026-10-08
A Chinese baby name score is a 100-point total built from seven checked parts: the child's favourable element (用神), the five grids (五格), the three talents (三才), meaning, sound, gender fit and data confidence. Each part has a fixed weight, so the final grade can be traced back to the rule behind every point.

## How is a name scored out of 100?

A name is rarely good or bad on one test. A character can carry the right element, have an excellent stroke count and still sound like something embarrassing. The builder at bazifor.me therefore scores seven parts, weights them, and adds them up. Nothing is hidden: the weights below are the ones the engine uses.

Part | Weight | What it checks | 

用神 | 30 | Does each character carry an element the child's chart needs? | 

五格 | 25 | Are the five stroke-count grids lucky or unlucky? | 

三才 | 15 | Do the elements of the heaven, person and earth grids support each other? | 

字义 | 10 | What do the characters mean, in 16 meaning categories? | 

音韵 | 5 | Do the tones and sounds read well, and do they collide with a bad word? | 

性别 | 5 | Does the name fit the child's gender, using character tags? | 

可信度 | 10 | How far can the engine trust the data behind the other parts? | 

The seven weights add up to 100. The sum of the weights is the highest total a name can reach.

Key facts

- The seven weights are 用神 30, 五格 25, 三才 15, 字义 10, 音韵 5, 性别 5 and 可信度 10.
- The grade bands are 90 and above 上佳, 80 and above 佳, 65 and above 可, and below 65 待斟酌.
- A strong sound hit (an English profanity, a homophone or a severe homophone) caps the grade at 待斟酌 whatever the total.
- The sound layer is backed by 303 sound-alike entries, of which 79 are severe, and 72 English reading checks.
- 478 characters carry meaning tags, in 16 meaning categories, and 171 characters carry gender tags.
- Strokes follow the 康熙字典 count, which uses the traditional form of each character.

## Why does 用神 carry the most weight?

Because it is the part that comes from the child, not from the name. The 用神 is the element the child's BaZi chart needs most, chosen by 扶抑, 調候, 通關 and 病藥. See what a useful god is for how it is found. A character carries an element, and the engine gives each character a role score against the child's chart:

- 用神 (the useful god): 1.0

- 喜 (favourable): 0.7

- 闲 (neutral) or 未定 (undetermined): 0.3

- 忌 (unfavourable): 0.0

The 30 points scale with these role scores (method note: the exact blending across characters is the engine's). That is why the child's birth moment matters for naming. The chart behind the 用神 depends on true solar time. For a birth in Singapore or Malaysia the clock is UTC+8 (UTC+7:30 in Singapore before 1982), and a birth near a two-hour boundary can change the hour pillar and with it the 用神. The year changes at 立春, so a late January or early February birth may belong to the previous year.

## How do the five grids (五格) work?

The 五格 are five numbers derived from the stroke counts of the surname and given name: the 天格 (heaven), 人格 (person), 地格 (earth), 外格 (outer) and 總格 (total) grids. Each number is looked up in the 81-number system (81數理), which marks it 吉 or 凶. This is a modern naming-school convention, not a classical rule, and the engine uses only the two-state 吉/凶 reading (method note).

Stroke counts come from the 康熙字典. This matters because the dictionary uses the traditional form: 祿 has more strokes than the simplified 禄, so a name typed in simplified Chinese must be counted in its traditional form.

The 25 points are split across the grids by name length:

Name type | 人格 | 地格 | 總格 | 外格 | Total | 

双名 (two-character given name) | 8 | 7 | 7 | 3 | 25 | 

单名 (one-character given name) | 15 | 10 | not scored | not scored | 25 | 

The 天格 is not scored in either layout: it comes from the surname alone, so no choice of given name changes it (method note).

## Which element relations count in the 三才?

The 三才 (three talents) are the elements of the 天格, 人格 and 地格. The engine reads the relation between the elements and gives each relation a factor:

Relation | Factor | 

生 (one generates the next) | 1.0 | 

比 (same element) | 0.8 | 

洩 (drain) | 0.4 | 

人剋 (the person element restrains) | 0.2 | 

被剋 (the person element is restrained) | 0.0 | 

The 15 points scale with these factors. The relations follow the five-element generating and restraining cycles shown below.

The five-element generating and restraining cycles used to read the 三才 relations: wood feeds fire, fire feeds earth, earth feeds metal, metal feeds water, water feeds wood

## How does the sound layer work?

The sound part is worth 5 points and starts from a full score. It subtracts penalties for patterns that make a name awkward to say, and for collisions with other words. The penalties are the engine's own (method note):

Pattern | Penalty | 

Same tone repeated | 0.4 | 

Two third tones together | 0.2 | 

Ending on a neutral tone | 0.2 | 

Same syllable repeated | 0.4 | 

Reduplication | 0.1 | 

Same initial | 0.2 | 

Same final | 0.2 | 

Cap on all repeat penalties together | 0.4 | 

Near-homophone of a bad word | 0.5 | 

Tone-different homophone | 0.7 | 

Homophone | 1.0 | 

Severe homophone | 1.0 | 

English tease | 0.5 | 

English profanity | 1.0 | 

Sound-alike checks run against 303 dictionary entries (79 of them severe) and 72 English reading checks. Three kinds of hit are strong: an English profanity, a homophone, and a severe homophone. A strong hit does more than lose points. It caps the grade at 待斟酌 whatever the total, because a name that sounds like a swear word is not rescued by lucky strokes. Weaker hits, such as a near-homophone or an English tease, only cost points.

## What does the meaning and gender layer add?

The 字义 part (10 points) looks up each character in a table of 478 tagged characters across 16 meaning categories. The result also produces a short interpretation of the name, written from those tags. The 性别 part (5 points) uses 171 gender tags, which check the name against the child's gender.

## What does a worked example look like?

Take the fictional girl's name 王禄婷 (traditional 王祿婷), for a child born on 2026-03-15 at 09:30.

- Strokes (康熙字典): 王 4, 祿 13, 婷 12.

- Five grids: 天格 5 (土), 人格 17 (金), 地格 25 (土), 外格 13 (火), 總格 29 (水). All five read 吉, so 五格 earns the full 25.

- 三才: 土 金 土. The engine's detail lines read 天土生人金 ×1.0 and 地土生人金 ×0.4, the verdict is 中, and the part earns 10.5 of 15.

- Sound: tones 2, 4, 2 (wang, lu, ting). There are no findings, so the part earns the full 5.0.

- The other parts: 用神 30.0, 字义 10.0, 性别 5.0 and 可信度 10.0.

The total is 30 + 25 + 10.5 + 10 + 5 + 5 + 10 = 95.5, which lands in the 上佳 (excellent) band. The only points lost are the 4.5 in the 三才 part. The engine's reading of the name is: 既福禄双全，又亭亭玉立, or "a name suggesting blessing and prosperity; graceful and poised."

A name scoring 89.9 would read 佳, one scoring 79 would read 可, and anything under 65 reads 待斟酌.

## How are the grades set?

Total | Grade | English | 

90 and above | 上佳 | excellent | 

80 to under 90 | 佳 | good | 

65 to under 80 | 可 | fair | 

under 65 | 待斟酌 | reconsider | 

"Reconsider" does not say the name is wrong for your family. It says the rules have found a reason to look again.

## Sources and method

- Stroke counts: the 康熙字典, in traditional character forms.

- 五格 grids and the 81 numbers: a modern naming-school convention (method note), with only the two-state 吉/凶 reading used.

- 三才 relations: the five-element generating and restraining cycles, with the factors above (method note).

- 用神: the four methods 扶抑, 調候, 通關 and 病藥, applied to the child's chart under the 子平 true-solar-time convention.

- Sound, meaning, gender and confidence parts, and the grade cap: the engine's own rules and data tables (method note), not classical sources.

Score a name for your own child in the baby name builder at /baby, with the full breakdown and the rule behind every part.

# Is BaZi Deterministic? Why We Compute Readings Instead of Chatting Them

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/is-bazi-deterministic
Updated: 2026-09-16

BaZi Basics

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-09-16
"AI fortune telling" is everywhere now: paste your birthday into a chatbot and receive a confident, fluent, unrepeatable reading. Ask twice, get two different answers. This article draws the line that industry blurs: which parts of BaZi are deterministic, which parts are interpretive, and why the difference should decide what tool you trust.

## Layer 1: the computation (fully deterministic)

The Four Pillars are calendar math. Solar terms, the 60-day 甲子 cycle, true solar time, the 立春 year boundary — every step has one correct answer. The same is true further up the stack than most people realize:

- Day Master strength assessment — seasonal weighting plus rooted support, by written rule.

- 用神 selection — the four classical techniques (扶抑, 调候, 病药, 通关) applied in a defined order.

- Ten Gods (十神) — each stem's relation to the Day Master is a fixed mapping.

- Luck cycles (大运) — start age and sequence are computed from the birth data.

- Eight House 命卦 and direction maps, flying-star charts, annual afflictions, 文昌 positions, even auspicious-date filtering (建除 officers, branch clashes) — all lookup and arithmetic.

A century ago this was a master's mental arithmetic; today it is an engine's job. Any two honest implementations must agree to the digit — and that is testable. Our engine is validated against a professionally produced paid audit, reproduced line by line.

## Layer 2: the interpretation (rule-guided, but written by humans)

What a weak 丁 fire with strong 官杀 means for your career is interpretation — but classical interpretation is not freeform either. The texts state patterns and their readings; a faithful system encodes those patterns and cites the rule behind every sentence it outputs. The sentence "metal drains your afflicted earth star, so keep this room's surfaces white or metallic" is checkable: the rule exists in the literature, the star was computed, the inference follows.

## Where chatbots go wrong

A large language model improvises text that sounds like a reading. Three failure modes follow: it miscomputes the pillars (calendar edge cases are exactly what LLMs fumble — 立春 boundaries, true solar time, pre-1982 Singapore clocks); it cannot show which rule produced a claim, because none did; and it is unrepeatable, so it cannot be validated against anything. Fluency is not method.

## Determinism is not fatalism

"Deterministic" describes the computation, not your life. The chart is a starting condition and a map of tendencies; the classical tradition itself insists on 一命二运三风水 — fate, then timing, then environment, and on down through education and effort. The reason to want an exact chart is precisely so that the actionable layers — colours, directions, dates, room choices — rest on solid ground instead of on a chatbot's mood.

Every reading on this site is generated by that rule engine — no LLM in the loop, every line citing its source. See yours below.

---

# Luck Cycles (大運) and Annual Windows: The Climate and Weather of a BaZi Chart

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/luck-cycles-and-windows
Updated: 2026-09-19

A birth chart is fixed; life is not. BaZi models time with two moving layers. The luck
cycles 大運 are ten-year pillars, derived from the month pillar and stepped forward or
backward by sex and year polarity — each decade overlays one stem and one branch on the natal
chart. The annual pillar 流年 changes every 立春 (around February 4th) and overlays one
more. The decade is the climate; the year is the weather inside that climate.

## Grading a decade

Each decade's two characters are read against the chart's favourable and unfavourable
elements, plus the interactions they form with the natal pillars (combinations, clashes,
punishments). The result is a phase label: a growth decade (both characters helpful), a corrective
one (both against the grain — a decade for maintenance, learning and pruning rather than big
bets), or consolidation and transition phases in between. Two habits keep this honest. First, a
corrective decade is not a bad life — it is a season with different work. Second, the decade
brings its own ten gods: a chart missing an authority star can
borrow one from a 官殺 decade for ten years, and behave accordingly.

## Annual windows — four dimensions

Within a decade, each year is checked per life dimension rather than given one verdict:
career (does the year activate or clash the month pillar; do authority stars arrive),
wealth (do wealth stars arrive — and can the chart hold them; is it a 財庫 vault-opening
year), relationship (桃花 peach-blossom years and activations of the spouse palace, the
day branch), and health (years that feed an excess or replenish a weak element). A window
is a tailwind, a caution is a navigation note; neither is a prediction.

## The vault, the peach blossom, and other timed stars

Some chart features exist only as timing: the wealth vault 財庫 is the storage branch of
your wealth element (one of 辰戌丑未) — present-but-sealed vaults open in their clash years, which
are classic accumulation windows. The peach blossom 桃花 branch governs attraction years;
the scholar star 文昌 favours exam and publication years. This is why two people with similar
charts diverge: their calendars strike different pillars at different ages.

Read the decade band first (where am I in the arc), then the current year's four flags,
then plan against the next green column — that is the whole method, and every flag in our readings
cites the rule that raised it.

---

# Choosing a Move-In Date (入宅择日): The Classical Method, Step by Step

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/move-in-date-selection
Updated: 2026-09-16

Dates

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-09-16
Date selection (择日) is the most immediately practical branch of the classical toolkit, and moving into a home (入宅) is its most requested application. It is also fully computable — a filter pipeline over the calendar, applied in a fixed order. Here is the method, exactly as an engine (or a careful almanac reader) runs it.

## Step 1: the twelve day officers (建除十二神)

Every day carries one of twelve officers, determined by the relationship between the day's branch and the month's branch. For moving in, three officers are the classic keepers:

- 成 (Completion) — the strongest choice: things established endure.

- 定 (Settling) — stability; excellent for taking residence.

- 开 (Opening) — beginnings; good, slightly behind the other two.

Days carrying 破 (Destruction), 闭 (Closing) and most others are simply passed over for this purpose. This first filter alone removes about three-quarters of the calendar.

## Step 2: strike the clash days (六冲)

Each Earthly Branch clashes with the branch opposite it (子↔午, 丑↔未, 寅↔申, 卯↔酉, 辰↔戌, 巳↔亥). Three clash checks apply:

- Every occupant's year branch. A day whose branch clashes any family member's birth-year branch is out — the move should not collide with anyone who will live there.

- The house's sitting (冲坐山). A day clashing the branch of the direction your home sits toward disturbs the foundation of the very thing you are establishing. (A sitting on a stem or trigram mountain borrows its palace's branch.)

- The year's 太岁 (值太岁). A day whose branch matches the year branch confronts the Grand Duke — also out.

## Step 3: the customs that complete it

With candidate dates in hand, tradition adds the finishing conventions: move in during the morning — the 巳时 block (9–11 am) is the customary favourite — carry something of value in first, and light the stove the same day: boil water, cook something simple. In the classical view the burning stove, not the furniture, is what declares occupancy. And if renovation preceded the move, the annual affliction sectors (太岁 / 岁破 / 三煞 / 五黄) should already have dictated when each room's work happened — date selection and renovation timing are two halves of one calendar discipline.

## Why weekends thin out

Run the full pipeline over a three-month window and you will typically keep six to twelve days — and only a couple land on weekends, which is why families who need a Saturday should scan a generous window early. The filters are unforgiving in a specific, checkable way: a large family protects more branches, so their calendar is thinner. That is not superstition compounding; it is set intersection.

Our engine runs exactly this pipeline for your household: it reads every family member's year branch from their charts, derives the sitting branch from your home's facing, and returns the clean 成/定/开 days in any window you choose — each exclusion explainable by the rule above. It is built into the home-fengshui workspace; start with the free reading below.

---

# Symbolic Stars (神煞) in BaZi: Noblemen, 文昌, 桃花 and What They Actually Add

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/shensha-symbolic-stars
Updated: 2026-09-19

神煞 symbolic stars are classical pattern-matches: fixed lookup tables that attach a
named star to a chart when particular stem-branch combinations occur. They are flavour ON TOP of
the structural reading — the element balance, ten gods and palaces do the heavy lifting; the
stars annotate it. A serious reading lists them with their pillar, because the pillar decides the
life-area and era the star colours (see
the four palaces).

## The stars worth knowing

- 天乙貴人 Heavenly Nobleman — the most valued: helpful people appear at critical
moments. Doubled Noblemen (two pillars) mark a chart that attracts rescuers.

- 文昌貴人 Scholar star — study, writing, exams; in the year pillar it colours early
schooling, in the hour pillar late-life scholarship. Its direction also gives the
study corner.

- 太極貴人 Tai Chi Nobleman — affinity for metaphysics, research, depth subjects.

- 將星 General star — command presence; leadership in the palace it occupies.

- 華蓋 Canopy — solitude, art, spiritual interests; gifted alone-time rather than
loneliness when the chart supports it.

- 桃花 Peach Blossom — attraction and social magnetism, mostly read through its YEARS
(see timing) when not in the natal chart.

- 劫煞 Robbery sha · 空亡 Void — the cautions: leak-prone moments, and a hollow pillar
whose promises need double-checking. Noted, not feared.

## How much weight to give them

Less than the structure, always. A Nobleman does not rescue a chart whose useful element is
buried, and a Void does not sink one whose structure is sound. The honest use of 神煞 is
descriptive precision: they give a name to textures people recognise in themselves — the friend
who always finds a helper, the student who tests as brilliant but studies alone. When a star and
the structure agree, say it once with confidence; when they disagree, the structure wins. That
ranking — structure first, stars as annotation — is itself classical doctrine, and it is how our
engine orders every reading it computes.

---

# The Ten Gods (十神) Explained: What You Have, What You Lack, and Why It Matters

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/ten-gods-guide
Updated: 2026-09-26

Once the Day Master is fixed, every other character in a BaZi chart — visible or hidden — falls
into one of ten relationships with it: the 十神 ten gods. They come in five pairs, one pair
for each of the five elemental roles, split by yin-yang polarity:

- 比肩 Friend · 劫財 Rob Wealth (peers 比劫) — self-identity, willpower, siblings,
competition.

- 食神 Eating God · 傷官 Hurting Officer (output 食傷) — expression, creativity,
critique; your life's output.

- 正財 Direct Wealth · 偏財 Indirect Wealth (wealth 財) — salary and savings;
opportunity and business flair.

- 正官 Direct Officer · 七殺 Seven Killings (authority 官殺) — rules, status, career,
discipline, pressure.

- 正印 Direct Resource · 偏印 Indirect Resource (resource 印) — learning, protection,
credentials, intuition.

The 正 gods are the conventional, steady flavour of each domain; their counterparts are the
intense, unconventional flavour — powerful when channelled, costly when not. The classical "four
benign" are 正官·正印·正財·食神; the "four fierce" are 七殺·傷官·偏印·劫財.

## Reading a distribution chart

A ten-god distribution chart weighs every visible and hidden stem and shows how the chart's
energy divides among the ten. Three habits make it useful. First, read the heavy bars as both
engine and watch-list: a god's shadow side activates when it is excessive or unsupported —
26% of 正官 is real authority and real self-imposed pressure. Second, read the empty bars:
a missing god is a life-domain that does not run on autopilot. No 比劫 means self-drive must be
deliberate; no 官殺 means structure has to be chosen, not imposed. Missing is not doomed — it is
unautomated. Third, percentages start the reading, structure finishes it: whether the
heavy god sits on a favourable element for you, whether it is rooted in a branch, and what the
gods form together (patterns like 傷官見官, talent chafing against authority) decide how the
weight actually behaves.

## The cycle as a tree

A memorable way to hold the five groups at once: 比劫 are the roots absorbing nutrients,
食傷 the branches and leaves that grow from them, 財 the flowers that set fruit, 官殺 the
pickers who arrive for the harvest, and 印 the soil that rests and recovers — feeding new
roots. Creation → accumulation → constraint → nourishment, around forever; every chart
simply weights the stations of this cycle differently.

## The gods as people

Each god also stands for people (六親): wealth gods for the father — and in a man's chart
the wife; authority gods in a woman's chart for the husband; resource for the mother and
mentors; output for students and, in a woman's chart, children; peers for siblings and rivals.
That is why the same distribution chart doubles as a relationship map, and why the spouse star's
strength and the spouse palace (the day branch) are read together.

## Gods arrive with time

The chart is the cast; the calendar is the schedule. Every stem maps to a god for your Day
Master, so each ten-year luck pillar and each passing year brings specific gods on stage. A decade
that carries your missing god supplies it for ten years; a year that doubles an already-heavy god
tests its shadow side. This is how a static birth chart produces a moving story — see
luck cycles and windows.

## Two sides of each god 双面性

Every god has a bright side and a shadow side. The shadow activates when the god is excessive or unsupported in a chart — read your prominent gods as both your engine and your watch-list.

God | Bright side 优 | Shadow side 忌 | 

正印 | broad learning, kindness, quiet support 学识渊博·仁慈包容·精神支持 | over-reliance, idealism, indecision 过度依赖·理想主义·缺决断 | 

偏印 | deep insight in niche fields, original self-taught skill 小众洞察·深度创新 | solitary, suspicious, keeps people at arm's length 孤僻多疑·疏离人际 | 

正官 | responsibility, order, stable social standing 责任感强·守序重诺·地位稳 | conservatism, rule-bound pressure and anxiety 循规保守·压力焦虑 | 

七殺 | leadership in adversity, execution, pioneering 逆境显领袖·执行力强 | impulsiveness; health and legal risks 冲动暴力·易招风险 | 

比肩 | confident, loyal, natural team player 自信独立·重义善团队 | stubborn over spoils, self-centred splits 固执争利·自我中心 | 

劫財 | strong social drive, dares to take risks 社交力强·敢于冒险 | impulsive losses, easily talked into traps 冲动失财·轻信陷骗局 | 

食神 | overflowing talent, easy-going, deep bond with children 才华横溢·豁达乐天 | comfort-seeking, weak follow-through, indulgence 贪图安逸·行动力弱 | 

傷官 | innovation, eloquence, artistic force 创新突破·口才卓越 | rebellious, attracts resentment, marriage friction 叛逆招怨·个性冲突 | 

正財 | diligence, steady income, loyalty 勤俭持家·收入稳定·婚姻忠诚 | stingy, conservative, material over spirit 吝啬保守·重物轻神 | 

偏財 | keen money sense, generosity, seizes windfalls 财运敏锐·慷慨善机遇 | extravagance, tangled romantic affairs 挥霍无度·情感纠纷 |

---

# Useful God (用神) in BaZi: Find Your Favourable Elements and Colours

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/useful-god-colors
Updated: 2026-10-08

BaZi Basics

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-10-08
A useful god (用神) is the element a BaZi chart needs most, chosen by rule from the balance of the Day Master and the season. Four classical methods find it: 扶抑, 調候, 通關 and 病藥. Once it is known, it turns into practical choices such as colours, directions and room use.

## How is the 用神 chosen?

After the Four Pillars are cast and the Day Master's strength is assessed, classical BaZi asks the most practical question in the system: which element does this chart need? The usual English, "useful god", is a little grand. "Operative element" is closer to the sense. Colours, directions, timing and even room choices in home feng shui flow from it.

The classical toolkit has four techniques, and the engine cites which one it used:

- 扶抑 (support and restrain) is the workhorse. A weak Day Master is supported by the element that generates it (印, the resource) and the element that matches it (比劫, peers). A strong one is drained or disciplined by output (食傷), wealth (財) or authority (官殺).

- 調候 (climate adjustment) looks at the season. A chart born in deep winter may need fire regardless of strength, and a blazing summer chart may need water. Season can override arithmetic when the imbalance is extreme.

- 通關 (bridging) applies when two camps of elements deadlock. The element that mediates between them unlocks the chart.

- 病藥 (illness and medicine) applies when one element dominates and distorts the chart. The element that checks it is the cure.

These are written rules, and two practitioners applying them honestly reach the same answer. That is why a deterministic engine can compute the 用神 and name the technique behind it. The strength framework underneath is 旺相休囚死 (how strong each element is in the birth month) together with 通根 (whether the Day Master has roots in the branches).

Key facts

- The 用神 is found by 4 techniques: 扶抑, 調候, 通關 and 病藥.
- The five elements each have 2 colour families in the engine: wood 綠 青, fire 紅 紫, earth 黃 棕, metal 白 金, water 黑 藍.
- In the engine's naming score, a name character that matches the 用神 earns 1.0, a 喜 element 0.7, a neutral one 0.3 and a 忌 element 0.0.
- The sample chart 戊辰 乙卯 己巳 戊辰 has a weak Day Master 己 (score -0.97), and its 用神 are fire and earth.
- The five-element cycles are fixed: wood feeds fire, fire feeds earth, earth feeds metal, metal feeds water, and water feeds wood.
- The 三命通會 is the classical source for the 扶抑 reasoning the engine cites.

The five-element generating and restraining cycles: wood feeds fire, fire feeds earth, earth feeds metal, metal feeds water, water feeds wood

## What does a worked example look like?

Take the fictional 王大明, a man born on 1988-03-15 at 09:30 Singapore clock time. True solar time for Singapore (UTC+8, longitude 103.8517°E, equation of time -9.4 minutes) is 08:16, so the hour pillar is counted in the 辰 block. The pillars are 戊辰, 乙卯, 己巳, 戊辰, and the Day Master is 己, yin Earth.

Strength. The month branch is 卯, wood, which restrains earth, so the Day Master is in the 死 phase. Support totals 6.33 against a drain of 3.67, and the roots (通根) are 辰, 巳 and 辰. The net score is -0.97: 身弱, weak.

Technique. Technique 1 of 4, 扶抑法, applies directly. A weak Day Master favours the resource element (印, Fire) and the peer element (比劫, Earth). Technique 2 of 4, 調候法, is also cited in the result. The 用神 come out as Fire and Earth. The unfavourable elements are Wood, Water and Metal.

Colours. The favourable families are 紅 and 紫 for fire, and 黃 and 棕 for earth.

Element | Role for 王大明 | Colour families | 

火 Fire | favourable (印) | 紅 紫 | 

土 Earth | favourable (比劫) | 黃 棕 | 

木 Wood | unfavourable | 綠 青 | 

水 Water | unfavourable | 黑 藍 | 

金 Metal | unfavourable | 白 金 | 

The roles are reproduced from the engine, so a different chart gives a different table. A strong Day Master is drained or disciplined instead of supported, so the favourable elements for such a chart come from a different group.

## Which colours should I actually use?

Your favourable elements' colours are worth favouring where you spend sustained time: wardrobe staples, bedding, a study corner, a phone case you see two hundred times a day. Your unfavourable elements' colours are not poison; they are simply not doing you any favours in bulk. The classical advice is dosage, not prohibition. An unfavourable colour as an accent is background noise; as the whole bedroom wall it is a standing weight.

In a Singapore or Malaysian home, three practical limits apply.

- Rented and HDB walls. A rented unit often cannot be repainted. Move the personal palette to what you can change: bedsheets, curtains, a rug, a lampshade and desk accessories.

- Large surfaces versus small ones. Paint a feature wall or a cabinet front in a favourable colour before changing a whole room, and keep unfavourable colours to accents.

- Room context. In home feng shui, a room's flying-star overlay can outrank the personal palette on walls and large surfaces, with the personal colours moving to textiles. Rules interact, and a good reading shows the precedence.

The same element logic reaches the bed direction guide, which uses your kua rather than your 用神 for direction, and the flying stars guide, which adds the annual overlay.

## Why do people get the 用神 wrong?

- Guessing from the Day Master alone. A water Day Master does not automatically "need" water. A strong 壬 usually needs the opposite, because strength decides the direction of the remedy.

- Treating the zodiac animal as the answer. The year branch is one-eighth of the chart.

- Using the wrong hour. The hour pillar comes from true solar time. In 王大明's case the clock reads 09:30 but the sun reads 08:16, which changes the hour from 巳 to 辰 and therefore the roots and the strength score.

- Using the wrong year for early February births. The year pillar changes at 立春, which is 2027-02-04 in 2027, and not at Chinese New Year.

- Pre-1982 births. Singapore ran on UTC+7:30 before 1982-01-01 and UTC+8 after; Peninsular Malaysia is UTC+8 from 1982-01-01. The conversion must be applied before any pillar is cast.

## Where else does the 用神 show up?

The same labels carry across the site. In the baby name builder, each character in a name is scored against the 用神 using the weights above (method note), and the 用神 is the largest single part of the score. See How Chinese baby names are scored for that.

## Sources and method

- Choosing the 用神: 扶抑, 調候, 通關 and 病藥 (the 用神 四法), cited by number in the engine's result.

- Weak or strong Day Master: the 旺相休囚死 and 通根 framework, scored numerically (method note).

- The 扶抑 reasoning (weak Day Master favours resource and peers): 三命通會, in its discussion of 用神 and 扶抑.

- Hour pillar conversion: the 子平 true-solar-time convention, with the UTC+7:30 and UTC+8 offsets applied first (method note).

- Colour families: the engine's table of two colour words per element (method note), not a classical list.

Compute your own favourable elements, with the technique cited, in the free reading at /start. To see the colours in a room plan, use the home tool at /fengshui.

# The 文昌 Study Corner: Where a Desk Works Hardest

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/wenchang-study-corner
Updated: 2026-09-16

Fengshui

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-09-16
Classical practice reserves a special direction for study and scholarship: 文昌, the scholar star. Unlike generic "study tips," 文昌 is personal and computable — it derives from your BaZi Day Master, so two children in the same family usually have different study corners. This is one of the most useful and least-known applications of a BaZi chart.

## How your 文昌 position is derived

Each of the ten Day Master stems maps to one Earthly Branch — 甲 to 巳, 乙 to 午, 丙 and 戊 to 申, 丁 and 己 to 酉, 庚 to 亥, 辛 to 子, 壬 to 寅, 癸 to 卯 — and each branch lives in a compass palace. Your 文昌 palace is where that branch sits on the compass. A 庚-metal student's scholar star is 亥, in the northwest palace; a 壬-water student's is 寅, in the northeast. Lookup, not intuition.

## Applying it in a real home

- Desk location: ideally, the desk sits in the room (or the corner of a room) that falls in your 文昌 palace.

- Chair facing: face one of your auspicious Eight House directions while working — 生气 for drive, 天医 for steadiness. Location and facing are two separate rules; the strongest setup satisfies both.

- The fallback rule (坐吉向吉): homes are finite, and someone's 文昌 palace is regularly occupied by a bathroom or someone else's bedroom. The classical fallback: sit anywhere solid and face an auspicious direction. An auspicious facing at a solid desk beats an awkward squeeze into the "correct" corner.

## The desk's own form rules

The bed's doctrine has a desk-sized sibling:

- Solid backing. A wall behind the chair (靠山) — authority and focus. A window at your back gets a high-backed chair as the manufactured substitute.

- Never sit with your back square to the door. The commanding-position rule applies at a desk even more than a bed — you work best when nobody can approach unseen. Door behind-diagonal is acceptable; square behind needs the high-back chair and a closed-door habit.

- Face the wall or face the room? Facing the wall is fine if the door lies to your side or diagonal. The one layout to refuse is wall-in-front plus door-square-behind.

- The annual bonus: each year the annual 4 star (文曲, the academic star) visits one sector — in 2027 it sits in the south. A reading corner there is a one-year tailwind, layered on top of your permanent 文昌.

## For families

Because 文昌 follows the Day Master, a family of five can have five different study palaces — allocating bedrooms and desk corners becomes a genuine optimization problem. That is precisely what our home-fengshui tool computes when you add your family and trace your floor plan: each person's 文昌 palace, which of your actual rooms falls in it, the fallback facing when it is occupied, and the desk position that survives the door-doctrine audit. Start with the free reading to find your own Day Master and 文昌 direction.

# BaZi (八字) Explained: Four Pillars, Day Master and True Solar Time

Source: https://bazifor.me/learn/what-is-bazi
Updated: 2026-10-08

BaZi Basics

By BaziMaster 2026-09-16 Updated 2026-10-08
BaZi (八字, "eight characters") is a Chinese calendar system that converts a birth moment into four pillars, each a Heavenly Stem over an Earthly Branch, using solar terms and true solar time. The day stem is the Day Master, the character that stands for you. The pillars are computed exactly; only the reading that follows needs interpretation rules.

## What are the four pillars?

BaZi is often called Chinese astrology, but its first step is a calendar computation. Your birth moment becomes four pairs of characters, the Four Pillars (四柱). Two people born at the same place and minute get the same eight characters, from every competent practitioner, every time.

Each pillar is one Heavenly Stem (天干) sitting on one Earthly Branch (地支):

- Year pillar (年柱) changes at 立春, the "start of spring" solar term, not at Chinese New Year and not on 1 January.

- Month pillar (月柱) is set by solar terms, so each "month" begins at an astronomical moment rather than a calendar date.

- Day pillar (日柱) comes from the 60-day 甲子 cycle. Its stem is the Day Master (日主).

- Hour pillar (時柱) is one of twelve two-hour blocks (時辰), counted on true solar time.

Ten stems and twelve branches combine into a 60-unit cycle (六十甲子), so the same day pillar returns every 60 days and the same year pillar every 60 years.

Key facts

- The year pillar changes at 立春, which falls on 2027-02-04 in 2027 (and on 2026-02-04 and 2028-02-04 in the neighbouring years).
- A chart has 4 pillars and 8 characters: 4 stems and 4 branches.
- Singapore clocks ran on UTC+7:30 before 1982-01-01 and on UTC+8 after it.
- Peninsular Malaysia has used UTC+8 since 1982-01-01, so the same correction applies to births there.
- The engine converts clock time to true solar time from longitude and the equation of time, following the 子平 convention.
- Day Master strength is judged with the 旺相休囚死 and 通根 framework.

Sample chart 戊辰 乙卯 己巳 戊辰 laid out as four pillars, with the day stem 己 marked as the Day Master

## How is a BaZi chart calculated?

The computation has three steps, and none of them involves judgement.

- Fix the moment on the sun's clock. A wall-clock time is a political convention. BaZi uses true solar time, which depends on how far your birthplace sits from the time-zone meridian and on the equation of time (the seasonal drift between sundial and clock). This is the 子平 time convention.

- Find the solar terms. The year turns at 立春 and each month turns at a 節 (a "joint" solar term). A person born on 2027-01-20 has the year pillar 丙午 and the month pillar 辛丑. A person born on 2027-02-10, after 立春, has the year pillar 丁未 and the month pillar 壬寅. Same Gregorian year, different pillars.

- Read the pillars off the 60-cycle. Each pillar is a stem-branch pair from the 甲子 cycle. For example, the day of 2027-01-20 is 己亥, and the day of 2027-02-10 is 庚申.

Branches also contain hidden stems (藏干), which is why two charts with similar surfaces can behave differently. From these mappings, classical technique derives the strength of the Day Master, the favourable elements (用神), the Ten Gods (十神) and the ten-year luck cycles (大運).

## What does a worked example look like?

Take the fictional person 王大明, a man born on 1988-03-15 at 09:30 Singapore clock time.

Step 1, true solar time. Singapore sits at longitude 103.8517°E, well west of the UTC+8 meridian, and on 15 March the equation of time is -9.4 minutes. The engine converts 09:30 on the clock to 08:16 true solar time. That matters: 09:30 falls in the 巳 block, but 08:16 falls in the 辰 block. Skip the correction and the hour pillar is wrong.

Step 2, the pillars. The engine returns 戊辰 (year), 乙卯 (month), 己巳 (day) and 戊辰 (hour). The Day Master is 己, yin Earth.

Step 3, strength. The month branch 卯 is wood, and wood restrains earth, so the Day Master is in the 死 phase of 旺相休囚死 (method note: the engine scores the phases numerically). Support totals 6.33 against a drain of 3.67, and the roots (通根) are 辰, 巳 and 辰. The net score is -0.97, so the chart is 身弱 (weak).

Step 4, what follows. A weak Day Master calls for support, so the 用神 are Fire and Earth, and the colour families that carry them are 紅 紫 黃 棕. His kua is 震, in the East group (東四命). The luck cycles run forward (順行) from 乙卯 and start at age 6.7, counted to the 清明 term. Each of these lines is one rule applied once, which is why the reading can cite it.

The five elements in this chart relate through two cycles, and the table below is the lookup the engine uses for both.

Element | Generates (生) | Restrains (剋) | Colour families | 

木 Wood | 火 | 土 | 綠 青 | 

火 Fire | 土 | 金 | 紅 紫 | 

土 Earth | 金 | 水 | 黃 棕 | 

金 Metal | 水 | 木 | 白 金 | 

水 Water | 木 | 火 | 黑 藍 | 

## Why does "deterministic" matter?

The computation is exact, and the interpretation follows written rules. When a reading says your Day Master is weak and fire and earth support you, that conclusion comes from a rule you can look up, not from a mood, a template or a chatbot. At bazifor.me every line of a reading cites the rule that produced it, because a claim you cannot check is marketing, not knowledge.

Deterministic does not mean fatalistic. A chart is a starting point. The same pillars read differently once luck cycles and annual years (流年) are layered on, and a person's choices are not in the chart at all.

## Which mistakes change the pillars in Singapore and Malaysia?

- Using Chinese New Year as the year boundary. The boundary is 立春, so someone born in late January or early February may belong to the previous year.

- Using the clock instead of the sun. In 王大明's case the correction is 74 minutes and moves the hour from 巳 to 辰.

- Ignoring the pre-1982 clock. A Singapore birth before 1982-01-01 was recorded on UTC+7:30. The engine applies that offset before it computes true solar time.

- Taking a birth time from memory. A time of "around 9" can sit in two different 時辰. If the hour is unknown, a reading should say which findings depend on it.

Flats and condominiums do not enter a BaZi chart; they enter the home layer of feng shui, where your Day Master's favourable elements and your kua become colours and directions for each room. See the favourable-elements guide and the bed direction guide for those steps.

## Sources and method

- Solar-term months and the 立春 year boundary: the 子平 calendar convention, with annual and monthly turns at the solar terms.

- Hour pillar: the 子平 true-solar-time convention, with the Singapore (UTC+7:30 before 1982, UTC+8 after) and Malaysian (UTC+8 from 1982) clock offsets applied before conversion (method note).

- Day Master strength: the 旺相休囚死 and 通根 framework, with a numeric score (method note).

- Favourable elements: the 用神 four methods 扶抑, 調候, 通關 and 病藥, numbered 1 to 4 in the engine's citations (扶抑 is technique 1, 調候 technique 2).

- Ten stems, branches and their combinations: 三命通會, in the chapters the engine cites on stem pairing, clashes and combinations.

To see your own four pillars with these conversions applied, run the free reading at /start.
